To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tonic HRV, a possible physiological marker for inhibitory capacity, predicts the exercise of self-control in the pre and the post actional phases of goal pursuit after failure experience.

1) Tonic heart rate variability (HRV) is positively associated with self control, 2) tonic HRV increases after failure experience, and 3) tonic HRV is positively associated with the exercise of self-control in the pre- and post-actional phase after failure.
tonic HRV is positively associated with self confidence in the actional phase, even after controlling the effect of neurosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how self control can be improved.
the role of tonic HRV in goal pursuit.
the question how the exercise of self-control in goal pursuit is affected by failure experiences and the physiological regulation of inhibitory processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a failure experience increases the exercise of pre and post action self control, and that this effect is mediated by tonic HRV.
the results of this study indicate that the exercise of self-control is positively associated with tonic heart rate variability.
the present study has shown that tonic HRV is positively associated with the exercise of self-control, but not with the perception of self-control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physiological marker tonic HRV is positively associated with the exercise of self-control in goal pursuit, even after controlling the effect of neurosis.
the physiological marker of inhibiting capacity, the tonic HRV, increases the exercise in self control in the goal pursuit after failure.
the physiological state of the body is a crucial factor for self regulation in goal pursuit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physiological measure of heart rate variability can be used to predict self control in a real life situation.
the exercise of self-control in goal pursuit is not only a matter of will power but also a matter of physiology.
the exercise of self-control is associated with tonic heart rate variability, a possible physiological marker for inhibitory capacity.
